cohort: The study included 17,785,980 patients who underwent cesarean section, natural spontaneous delivery, or instrumental delivery between 2016 and 2020, comparing 6,000 patients with a secondary diagnosis of atrial fibrillation to those without.
finding: Patients with atrial fibrillation during delivery had almost 20 times higher odds of in-hospital mortality, stayed 1.5 days longer, incurred significantly higher costs, and had increased rates of blood transfusions and respiratory failure requiring intubation compared to patients without atrial fibrillation.
